title: Knowledge before the text
statement: Build the topic knowledge a hard text assumes, and give it before the reading, not after.
detail: An intro-video BrainLift for a Grade 3 reading course rests on two classic studies (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`): prior knowledge of baseball predicted memory for a baseball text on essentially every measure while general reading ability predicted almost none (Recht and Leslie 1988, line 439), and context given before an opaque passage transformed comprehension and recall while the same context given after did not (Bransford and Johnson 1972, line 446). Everything that document argues rests on its video sitting before the read (line 421). A BrainLift on early reading comprehension says comprehension rests on language and, more than anything, background knowledge (Catts 2021-2022; `downloads/WF - Brainlift Opportunities to - 260724-110911.md`, line 32), and the course's Grade 3 to 12 thematic map orders its texts so that earlier ones build the knowledge later ones need (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Curriculum maps/1. Mapping Docs/Grade_3-12_Full_Thematic_Map.xlsx`, sheet 'How to read this', cell A3). The sources give no links for these studies; the DOIs and the article's address were found on Crossref and the publisher's site.
against: Each finding is one classic study, and the Bransford and Johnson passages were written to be opaque without their context. Inside a text not all background has to come first: in the film study behind Background at the line that needs it, only 6 of 26 background points had to come before the first line.
